summary: Five items shipped this week: the blog with five pregnancy and baby posts, the postpartum recovery page, and new Google titles for the sports injury, sciatica and acupuncture pages.

Early signs are good: the sports injury page now shows up in the estimated results for three sports searches (#1, #3 and #4), and the sciatica page for “sciatica osteopath christchurch” (#5). Google's own numbers only run to 25 Sep, so they don't show these changes yet.
Clicks from people not searching for Meridian by name were 148 in the last 28 days, up from 140. The next gap is the back pain page, which Google shows at about position 28.

topActions.text: Approve #43 and click Ship it. Claude adds “Christchurch” to the back pain, neck pain and headache pages' Google titles, as already done for sciatica.
Approve the ACC page (#25) and click Ship it. Claude drafts it, then Nina checks the ACC wording before it goes live.
Nina: in Search Console, ask Google to index the blog and the five posts and the postpartum page (#44). About 10 minutes.

tldr: Google data (Search Console, last 28 days to 25 Sep vs the 28 days before): 254 clicks (279 before) from 4,196 appearances in Google (4,272). The fall is in name searches (“meridian osteopathy” 63 clicks, down from 114). Clicks from people not searching for Meridian by name rose from 140 to 148, and 32 searches show Meridian on Google's first page, up from 26. “Osteopath christchurch” improved from position 9.4 to 6.4 (174 appearances, 4 clicks). The homepage slipped from 6.5 to 9.4 on average. The sports injury page reached position 8 for “sports injury treatment” but still had no clicks; its new title only went live on 25–26 Sep, so next week's numbers are the real test.

Estimated ranks (a US-based web search, not what someone in Christchurch sees): 30 searches checked. New this week: the sports injury page is #1 for “sports injury recovery christchurch”, #3 for “sports injury osteopath christchurch” and #4 for “osteopath for sports injury christchurch” (all absent last week). The sciatica page appeared at #5 for “sciatica osteopath christchurch”, and the homepage at #4 for “paediatric osteopath christchurch”. The pregnancy back pain page held #1 on both wordings. The new postpartum page and blog posts don't appear yet for “postnatal” or “postpartum osteopath christchurch”. Better Health's ACC page has moved up to #1 for “osteopath acc christchurch”.

Pool changes: added “sciatica treatment” and “acupuncture riccarton” from Search Console, and “acupuncture christchurch price” and “treatment for sciatica nz” from Google's autocomplete. Dropped four low-signal searches. Google's spam update started on 24 Sep and can take two weeks, so small ranking moves until about 8 Oct may be noise. Shipped and removed from the list: #14 (blog), #36 (postpartum page), #40, #41 and #42 (Google titles for sports injury, sciatica and acupuncture).

gaps.title: No ACC landing page
gaps.why: Meridian still has no /acc/ page. Better Health's ACC page has moved up to estimated #1 for “osteopath acc christchurch”, ahead of Active Health. Item #25 covers it, using the “ACC-registered provider” wording from July (PR #113).

gaps.title: Blog started; needs regular posts
gaps.why: The blog launched on 28 Sep with five pregnancy and baby posts (item #14 shipped). They aren't visible in search yet. Competitors such as Better Health and osteopath-christchurch.com rank with one page per topic, so the gap is now keeping posts coming on topics people already search for. Item #45 suggests the next one.

gaps.title: No off-site citation strategy
gaps.why: Reddit is a major AI-citation source but the platform mix shifted sharply in the Jul-Aug window. UNCHANGED 2026-09-18: no material movement in the Reddit-Perplexity litigation / licensing situation since 31 Jul motion-to-dismiss rejection. Between Jul 1 and Aug 19, 2026, Perplexity supplied 71% of tracked Reddit citations while ChatGPT supplied 23%; ChatGPT Search citations linking to Reddit fell from ~250/day in early Aug to 16/day the week after Aug 14 — a -94% decline in six days. Reddit's Perplexity share is now ~24%, Gemini 0.1%. Item #15 stays on the backlog scoped to Perplexity-visibility only (larger share, smaller more curated source pool means single well-structured posts can surface); skip the ChatGPT-oriented seeding. 90/10 rule still applies: 90% non-promotional, 2–4 weeks of karma-building before any mention of Meridian.

items.title: Add speakable blocks on service intros
items.why: Unlikely to move your rankings. Google has kept this feature in test mode for years, and a large 2026 study found that adding this kind of behind-the-scenes code gave no real lift. It's cheap, but a good one to dismiss.
items.body: Wrap the short answer at the top of each service page in “speakable” code, which marks the text a voice assistant should read aloud. Google has kept speakable in test mode for years, and a 2026 study of 1,885 pages found that adding this kind of behind-the-scenes code made no clear difference to AI or search visibility. The best predictor of being quoted by AI is ranking well in normal Google results. Cheap to do, but low value; a reasonable one to dismiss.

items.title: Auto-fetch Google Business Profile reviews at build time
items.why: Up-to-date review numbers on your own site help visitors trust you, but they don't change your Google ranking by themselves. Getting new Google reviews (#16) is what moves rankings. It also needs a paid Google Places key set up first.
items.body: Pull the Google review count and star rating into the site at build time, so the numbers on the site stay current without manual edits. Needs a Google Places API key (a paid Google Cloud account) set up by the clinic first. Fresh reviews matter a lot for Google Maps rankings, but showing the count on the website doesn't change rankings by itself; getting new reviews (#16) does. Pairs well with #16 once reviews are flowing.

items.title: Answer local Reddit questions to show up in Perplexity AI search
items.why: Reddit mentions mainly help with the Perplexity AI search tool, which few NZ patients use. Time-consuming and hard to measure, so low priority.
items.body: Genuine, helpful answers in NZ Reddit threads (r/chch, r/newzealand) about osteopathy, ACC and back pain, with very occasional mentions of Meridian after weeks of ordinary participation. This mainly helps with Perplexity, an AI search tool few NZ patients use; ChatGPT cites Reddit much less since August. Time-consuming and hard to measure, so low priority.

items.title: Ask happy patients for Google reviews and reply to every review within 48 hours
items.why: Regular new Google reviews, answered within a day or two, are one of the best-proven ways for a local clinic to rank higher in Google Maps results.
items.body: Send a short email after each appointment asking happy patients for a Google review, using the email system the site already has. Reply to every review within a day or two, naming the practitioner or treatment the reviewer mentioned rather than using a template. Recent reviews carry the most weight in Google Maps rankings (Whitespark's 2026 study rates review recency as the top individual local factor), and Google's AI answers also draw on review text. Aim for about one new review a week.

items.title: Build an ACC page: Active Health and Better Health already have one
items.why: People search for ACC osteopaths, and Better Health (now estimated #1) and The House of Acupuncture both have dedicated ACC pages. Meridian doesn't appear for these searches yet. ACC wording is sensitive (see July's rewording), so Nina should check it.
items.body: A single page at /acc/ explaining ACC for patients. Estimated ranks for “osteopath acc christchurch”: Better Health's ACC page #1, Active Health #2. For acupuncture, The House of Acupuncture has a dedicated ACC page, and Google's autocomplete suggests “is acupuncture covered by acc” and “osteopath christchurch acc”. The page should say that Meridian is an ACC-registered provider (osteopathy with Nina Hu, acupuncture with Min Jin), what a patient pays, that no referral is needed, and that Meridian isn't part of ACC, with a link to acc.co.nz. Don't describe filing claims on the patient's behalf (see the July Google Ads rewording). Lead with a short 40–60 word answer, as on the condition pages.

items.title: Add a concussion page (only if someone at Meridian treats concussion)
items.why: Check first: none of your practitioners lists concussion as a special interest. Only build this page if someone at Meridian treats concussion and is happy to be named on it. Otherwise, dismiss it.
items.body: A /conditions/concussion/ page built like the existing condition pages. Estimated ranks for “concussion osteopath christchurch”: osteo.co.nz #1, Better Health #2 (through an associate osteopath's profile) and Triskelion Concussion Care #3. Meridian isn't visible, and Search Console shows no concussion searches reaching the site. Post-concussion symptoms (headaches, dizziness, neck pain) overlap with conditions Meridian already treats, but no practitioner lists concussion as a special interest. Confirm someone treats it and is happy to be named before building.

items.title: Check Google's AI Overviews report in Search Console and save a baseline
items.why: Search Console is now connected to this dashboard. The remaining step is a 5-minute look at Google's AI report, so you can later tell whether new pages show up in AI answers.
items.body: Search Console is connected and feeding this dashboard. Its separate AI report (appearances in AI Overviews and AI Mode) isn't pulled in automatically. In Search Console, open Performance, pick the AI features view, set the date range to the last 3 months, and save a screenshot as the “before” picture ahead of any new pages. The report shows appearances only, not clicks. Google's spam update started on 24 Sep and can take two weeks, so give it until mid-October before reading much into changes. Taking the screenshot now also captures a “before” picture for the new blog posts. No website changes needed.

items.title: Add “Christchurch” to the back pain, neck pain and headache page titles
items.why: Google shows the back pain page at about position 28 for “back pain christchurch” (51 appearances, no clicks). The same title change on the sciatica page was followed by an estimated #5 for “sciatica osteopath christchurch” within a week.
items.body: The three pages' Google titles are “Back Pain Treatment”, “Neck Pain Treatment” and “Headache & Migraine Treatment”, with no place name, and their main headings are just the condition name. Give each a title in the form “Back Pain Treatment in Christchurch | Meridian Osteopathy” (as the sciatica and sports injury pages now have) and make the main heading say “… treatment”. Search Console: back pain page position 27.9 (67 appearances), “osteopath for neck pain” 12.5, “headache clinic christchurch” 24.3, “osteopath for migraines” 27.1. Better Health ranks with titles like “Back Pain Treatment Christchurch”. Wording only, no clinical changes.

items.title: Ask Google to index the new blog posts and postpartum page
items.why: The blog and postpartum page went live on 28 Sep but don't show up yet for “postnatal” or “postpartum osteopath christchurch”. Asking Google to index them takes about 10 minutes and can speed up how soon they appear.
items.body: In Search Console, paste each new address into the search bar at the top (URL inspection) and click “Request indexing”: /blog/, the five posts under /blog/ and /conditions/postpartum-recovery/. Then open Sitemaps and resubmit /sitemap.xml, which already lists them. Estimated ranks for “postnatal osteopath christchurch” and “postpartum osteopath christchurch” are led by Better Health, osteo.co.nz and osteopath-christchurch.com, and Meridian isn't visible yet. Check the Pages report in two weeks to confirm they're indexed.

items.title: Next blog post: a plain guide to sciatica, checked by Jonathan
items.why: The sciatica page gets the most Google appearances of any condition page (242 in 28 days) but sits around position 29 overall. A practical article answering common sciatica questions gives Google a second, linked page on the topic.
items.body: A short post answering what people search for: “treatment for sciatica nz”, “sciatica specialist” (Search Console position 11), “can an osteopath help with sciatica” and “exercises for sciatica nz” (Google autocomplete). Cover how long sciatica usually lasts, when to see someone urgently, and what a first visit looks like, then link to the sciatica page. Jonathan lists sciatica as a special interest, so he should check the clinical content. Experimental because the blog is brand new and no post has ranked yet; read the result in Search Console about six weeks after publishing.
